item.title: UDP protocol analysis
item.description: UDP is the transport that sends one datagram and then forgets it. The datagram is an 8-byte header and a payload, and the network may drop it or deliver it out of order. HTTP/3 puts QUIC in that payload, so a request is a QUIC stream inside a UDP datagram.

item.title: WebSocket protocol analysis
item.description: WebSocket carries full-duplex messages on one TCP connection. The connection opens with an HTTP upgrade, then both peers exchange masked or unmasked frames until a close frame ends the session.

item.title: Introduction to Domain Name System
item.description: Domain Name System(DNS) is a hierarchical and distributed name service that provides a naming system for computers, resources and other resources on the IP network.

item.title: HTTP the application-layer protocol
item.description: HTTP is the application protocol of the request and the response. HTTP/1.1 writes that exchange as text on a TCP connection. HTTP/2 carries the same methods, headers, and bodies as binary frames, many streams at once, on one connection.
